content: The ACC 2015 schedule outlines the coordination of TV events during the conference, which will take place at the Manchester Grand Hyatt, located at 1 Market Street, San Diego, CA 92101. Open time slots are marked in red, and specific interviews with medical experts are scheduled as follows: Saturday, March 14, 2015 2:00 PM: Dr. Nicolai Tegn will discuss the After Eight Study. The embargo on this topic will lift on Monday, March 16, 2015, at 11:45 AM. Sunday, March 15, 2015 9:00 AM: Dr. Philippe Généreux will provide a wrap-up of ACC 2015 in French. 11:00 AM: Dr. Luigi Di Biase will present findings on Ablation vs. Amiodarone for Treatment of Persistent Atrial Fibrillation in Patients with Congestive Heart Failure and an Implanted Device, based on results from the AATAC Multicenter Randomized Trial. The embargo lifts on Monday, March 16, 2015, at 8:00 AM. 11:30 AM: Dr. Derek J. Hausenloy will discuss the Effect of Remote Ischemic Preconditioning on Clinical Outcomes in Patients Undergoing Coronary Artery Bypass Graft Surgery, a multicenter randomized controlled clinical trial. The embargo lifts on Monday, March 16, 2015, at 9:00 AM. 1:00 PM: Dr. Giora Weisz will address the impact of the PEGASUS Trial on clinical practice. 1:30 PM: Dr. Michael J. Mack will present the five-year outcomes after randomization to transcatheter or surgical aortic valve replacement, based on the final results of the PARTNER 1 Trial. The embargo lifts on Sunday, March 15, 2015, at 10:45 AM. 2:00 PM: Dr. Paul Sorajja will discuss the outcomes of the initial experience with commercial transcatheter mitral valve repair in the United States. The embargo lifts on Sunday, March 15, 2015, at 11:45 AM. 2:30 PM: Dr. David E. Newby will present on Computed Tomography Coronary Angiography in Patients with Suspected Angina Due to Coronary Heart Disease. The embargo lifts on Sunday, March 15, 2015, at 8:45 AM. 3:00 PM: Dr. Freek W. A. Verheugt will provide a wrap-up of ACC 2015 from the perspective of the Netherlands. 3:30 PM: Dr. Alexandra J. Lansky will report on the first results of the DEFLECT III Trial, a prospective randomized evaluation of the TriGuard™ HDH Embolic Deflection Device during transcatheter aortic valve replacement. The embargo lifts on Sunday, March 15, 2015, at 11:30 AM. 4:00 PM: Dr. Basil Lewis will provide a wrap-up of ACC 2015 in Hebrew. 4:30 PM: Dr. Michael J. Reardon will present a randomized comparison of self-expanding transcatheter and surgical aortic valve replacement in patients with severe aortic stenosis deemed at increased risk for surgery, focusing on two-year outcomes. The embargo lifts on Sunday, March 15, 2015, at 11:00 AM. 5:00 PM: Dr. Seung-Jung Park will discuss Everolimus-Eluting Stents versus Bypass Surgery for Multivessel Coronary Artery Disease. The embargo lifts on Monday, March 16, 2015, at 8:45 AM. Monday, March 16, 2015 8:30 AM: Dr. Renato Lopes will provide a wrap-up of ACC 2015 in Portuguese. 10:00 AM: Dr. Philip A. Aylward will present a wrap-up of ACC 2015 from the perspective of the Pacific Rim. 10:30 AM: Dr. Daniel B. Mark will discuss the economic comparison of anatomic versus functional diagnostic testing strategies in symptomatic patients with suspected coronary artery disease, based on results from the PROMISE Trial. The embargo lifts on Sunday, March 15, 2015, at 9:00 AM. 11:00 AM: Dr. Marc Gillinov will present on the effectiveness of surgical ablation of atrial fibrillation during mitral valve surgery, based on a randomized clinical trial from the Cardiothoracic Surgical Trials Network. The embargo lifts on Monday, March 16, 2015, at 8:15 AM. 11:30 AM: Dr. Rajeev K. Pathak will discuss the long-term effect of goal-directed weight management on an atrial fibrillation cohort, based on a five-year follow-up study (LEGACY Study). The embargo lifts on Monday, March 16, 2015, at 8:30 AM. 12:30 PM: Dr. Rino Sardella will provide a wrap-up of ACC 2015 in Italian. 1:00 PM: Dr. Hisao Ogawa will provide a wrap-up of ACC 2015 in Japanese. 1:30 PM: Dr. Susheel Kodali will present early clinical and echocardiographic outcomes with the SAPIEN 3 Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement System in inoperable, high-risk, and intermediate-risk aortic stenosis patients. The embargo lifts on Sunday, March 15, 2015, at 11:15 AM. 2:30 PM: Dr. Pamela S. Douglas will discuss a randomized comparison of anatomic versus functional diagnostic testing strategies in symptomatic patients with suspected coronary artery disease, based on results from the PROMISE Trial. The embargo lifts on Saturday, March 14, 2015, at 9:05 AM. 3:00 PM: Dr. Marco Valgimigli will present on transradial versus transfemoral access in patients with acute coronary syndromes undergoing invasive management, based on results from the MATRIX Program. The embargo lifts on Monday, March 16, 2015, at 11:00 AM and 11:15 AM, respectively. 3:30 PM: Dr. Marc Steven Sabatine will discuss the prevention of cardiovascular events in patients with prior heart attacks using ticagrelor compared to placebo on a background of aspirin (PEGASUS-TIMI 54) and the effect of the PCSK9 inhibitor evolocumab on cardiovascular outcomes. The embargo lifts on Saturday, March 14, 2015, at 9:30 AM and Sunday, March 15, 2015, at 8:00 AM, respectively. 4:00 PM: Dr. Roxana Mehran will present a randomized, open-label, multicenter, active-controlled, parallel group study to determine the efficacy and safety of the REG1 Anticoagulation System compared to bivalirudin in patients undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention. The embargo lifts on Sunday, March 15, 2015, at 8:30 AM. 4:30 PM: Dr. Thomas Engstrøm will discuss the third Danish study of optimal acute treatment of patients with ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction: primary PCI in multivessel disease. The embargo lifts on Monday, March 16, 2015, at 11:30 AM. This detailed schedule provides a comprehensive overview of the planned interviews and topics, along with embargo details for each presentation.
